name: LineChart
intent: How values change over time as lines or filled areas, one per series, like revenue by month or invoices approved by day.
usage: Use LineChart for trends across ordered categories, usually time. It is one component: pass categories (the labels along the bottom) and series (one values array each). area fills under each line; stacked piles the areas on each other so the top edge is the total, like invoices by severity. showPoints marks each value with a dot and showValues writes it above. A limit or target goes in referenceLines, a dashed line across the chart with its label and value at the end. A forecast stays in the same series: projectedFrom names its first forecast category, and the line turns dashed from there. marker draws a thin line down the chart at one category, like Today. Hover or use the arrow keys for a tooltip with every series at that point. animate plays a subtle draw-in. Put the chart's title and report link in the Section or Card around it. ChartIntent: green | olive | cyan | orange | pink | gray | purple | yellow | red | mint (the kit category colors). title and subtitle write a heading over the chart; showHeader turns it off when the Card around it already says the same. The keys under the chart are the kit Legend; legendPosition moves them over it or beside it. See contracts/linechart.json for the full contract. A legend beside the chart drops under it when the chart's own box is narrower than 360px. A reference label keeps clear of the marker's label, other reference labels and the points near the end of a line: it moves to the other side of its line, or slides left, rather than drawing over them.

label.note: Names the chart for screen readers and captions its data table, like Revenue by period.

title.note: Visible title over the chart, like Revenue by period. The screen-reader name still comes from label.

subtitle.note: A quieter line under the title, like Last 12 months, all accounts.

showHeader.note: Shows the title and subtitle. Off draws the chart alone, when the Card or Section around it already carries the title.

categories.note: The labels along the bottom, like Jan to Jun. Labels thin out when they would overlap.

series.itemShape: { name: string; values: number[]; intent?: ChartIntent; projectedFrom?: number }
series.note: One entry per line or bar color, with one value per category. intent picks the color; by default series take green, olive, cyan, orange, pink, gray, then purple, yellow, red and mint. projectedFrom is the first category that is a forecast, counted from 0: the line is dashed from the last actual point on, and the tooltip and table say projected.

area.note: Fills under each line. Overlapping areas are see-through.

stacked.note: Piles each series on the ones before it, as filled areas; the top edge is the total.

showPoints.note: A white dot with a colored ring at each value.

showValues.note: The short value above each point. For a few points only.

showGrid.note: Faint lines at each value tick.

showLegend.note: Colored squares with the series names under the chart.

legendPosition.note: Where the keys sit: under the chart, over it, or in a column beside it.

animate.note: Subtle motion when the chart appears. Off draws it at once. Always off when the person prefers reduced motion.

format.note: How values read. Axis ticks and value labels are short ($4.2M, 750K); the tooltip and table show the full number.

height.note: Height of the drawing in px, axis labels included. The width fills the container.

emptyLabel.note: Shown when there are no categories or series.

referenceLines.itemShape: { value: number; label: string; intent?: ChartIntent }
referenceLines.note: Dashed lines across the chart at a value, like a limit or a target. label names it, like Limit; the chart writes the short value after it, at the end of the line. Neutral gray unless intent picks a color. The scale always reaches the highest line.

marker.note: A thin line down the chart at one category, counted from 0, with its label over the top, like Today.

useWhen: Trends over time: revenue by month, approvals by day, a burndown.
Part-to-whole over time with stacked areas.
A limit, target or budget across a trend, like API calls against the plan limit: referenceLines.
Actual values and a forecast in one line: projectedFrom on the series, with a marker at today.
doNot: Do not use it for categories without an order, like regions. Use BarChart.
Do not use it for one share of a total. Use PieChart.
Do not fake a limit or target with an extra series. It shows in the legend, the tooltip and the table as data. Use referenceLines.
Do not draw a forecast as a second series. Use projectedFrom, so actual and forecast stay one line with one name.
Do not use marker for ranges or several moments. It marks one category, like today.
Do not draw charts with loose SVG or a chart library. Use the kit charts.
Do not use raw hex; pick an intent.
a11y: A figure named by label. The drawing is hidden from screen readers; a visually hidden table holds every value, with the categories as rows and the series as columns.
Reference lines and the marker are listed after the table for screen readers, like Limit: 10,000 and Today: Sep 13. Forecast values say projected in the tooltip and the table.
The chart takes focus: the arrow keys (and Home and End) move through the categories and show the same tooltip as pointing at them. Escape hides it.
Colors come with a legend and the tooltip names each series, so color is not the only way to tell them apart.
Motion is subtle and optional (animate), and never plays when the person prefers reduced motion.
snippet:
<LineChart
  label="Revenue by period"
  categories={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]}
  series={[{ name: "Revenue", values: [3.4e6, 3.6e6, 4.2e6, 4.4e6, 4.6e6, 4.9e6] }]}
  format="currency"
  area
  showPoints
  showValues
/>
